parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module is mostly a cohesive set of order/stock use cases that share OrderDto and toOrderDto. The problem is the order-status validation rule: it is written out three times instead of living in one place. AdvanceOrderUseCase.execute checks isOrderStatus and throws DomainError("VALIDATION", ...). ListOrdersUseCase.execute checks the same rule with the message "Query parameter 'status' must be a valid order status". AdvanceOrderUseCase also has a public validateExecute(status) that copies the ListOrders check word for word, message included. That message is about list-query parameters, so the copy sits in the wrong use case. It is also never called by execute, which makes it a separate, redundant entry point for the same rule. This breaks the "keep each rule or invariant in one place" part of the rubric. A smaller point: StockLevelDto lives in order-dto.ts, and GetStockLevelsUseCase builds the DTO inline instead of using a mapper the way the order use cases do. That is a slight mismatch in boundaries but would not fail the unit on its own.

violations.message: validateExecute copies ListOrdersUseCase's status-validation rule word for word, including the list-specific "Query parameter 'status'" message. execute does not call it and repeats the same isOrderStatus check itself, so the order-status validation rule exists in several places.
execute writes out the isOrderStatus validation and error message, and AdvanceOrderUseCase.validateExecute duplicates it instead of both using one shared check.
